chief_complaint: Metabolic risk management (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension) compounded by psychosocial stressors (intimate partner abuse, social isolation).
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 52-year-old woman with longstanding obesity (onset 1997) and prediabetes (onset 1987) who now has stage 1 hypertension (SBP 132/DBP 84). She reports chronic stress since 2017, social isolation and part-time employment since 2019, and has been a victim of intimate-partner abuse since early 2020. No pharmacologic therapy has been documented for her metabolic conditions. The most recent encounter was in April 2020 for colon polyp removal; there are no recent lipid, renal function, or repeat glucose labs. She is not taking any medications and has no recorded allergies. The record lacks data on smoking, alcohol use, physical activity, and detailed BMI, limiting full risk assessment.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include gingivitis and primary dental caries (2020, 2019), a colon polyp removed in 2020, multiple traumatic injuries (lacerations of thigh and knee, knee injury, patellar tendon rupture in 2016‑2017), acute bronchitis resolved in 2017, and a prior episode of stress resolved in early 2017. Full-time employment resolved in 2019.
social_determinants: Intimate partner abuse, social isolation, part-time employment (potential low income), and higher education status. No documented smoking, alcohol, or substance use.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 132/84 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension), heart rate 90 bpm, A1c 6.1% (prediabetic). BMI is recorded only as ≥30; exact value missing. Lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL) and eGFR are absent, preventing full ASCVD and renal risk calculation. Charlson comorbidity index is 0, but clinical complexity is flagged as moderate due to psychosocial stressors. Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (obesity, hypertension, prediabetes), metabolic/endocrine (prediabetes, obesity), renal (potential CKD risk without labs), mental health/behavioral (stress, abuse, isolation).

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing; only categorical obesity noted.
Lipid panel not available; limits ASCVD risk assessment.
No information on exercise or activity level.
No active prescriptions documented despite clear indications for antihypertensive, lipid‑lowering, or glucose‑lowering therapy.

clinical_impression: A middle‑aged woman with high metabolic risk (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension) and significant psychosocial stressors (intimate partner abuse, social isolation) who is not currently receiving pharmacologic treatment and lacks recent key laboratory data. The combination of metabolic and psychosocial factors places her at moderate‑to‑high risk for future cardiovascular disease, progression to type 2 diabetes, and mental‑health complications, warranting comprehensive risk‑factor management and psychosocial support.
